articles.title: FRAND at the Pool Level
articles.content:
英国最高法院今天上午一致裁定支持特斯拉对Avanci 5G许可平台收取的专利使用费的挑战，并认为特拉华州法院无法管辖此案。特斯拉公司诉InterDigital专利控股公司案（[2026] UKSC 27，2026年7月27日）。大法官汉布伦和基钦联名撰写判决书，塞尔斯大法官、布里格斯大法官和伯罗斯大法官表示同意。该判决推翻了分裂的上诉法院判决，并基本采纳了阿诺德法官的异议意见。其中，关于管辖权的裁定最有可能引起美国读者的兴趣。特斯拉母公司、InterDigital实体及Avanci均为美国公司，被告曾表示愿意接受特拉华州法院管辖，但法院仍裁定特拉华州法院无法管辖，认为美国法院可能不会为英国专利设定FRAND（公平、合理且无歧视）费率。

**英国最高法院背景**：该法院由2005年《宪法改革法案》创建，自2009年10月起运作，接管了英国议会上院的司法职能，是英格兰、威尔士、苏格兰和北爱尔兰民事案件的终审法院。法院设十二名大法官（称呼为大法官而非法官），多数案件由五名大法官组成的合议庭审理。上诉许可通常由三名大法官基于文件审查决定，下级法院也可授权。本案中上诉法院拒绝了特斯拉的上诉请求；最高法院则予以批准。

Avanci并不拥有任何标准必要专利（SEP），而是运营一个专利池（称为平台），作为89家拥有SEP的公司（包括InterDigital）的代理机构。这些公司均曾向ETSI（负责5G规范的欧洲组织）承诺，以公平、合理且无歧视的条件授权其必要专利。Avanci向汽车制造商提供单一全球许可证，覆盖整个专利池，按每辆车固定费率（判决举例使用32美元）收费，且不具备授权任何子集的合同权限。上诉法院多数法官认为，每家公司仅承诺以FRAND条件授权其自身专利，而未就整个池的价格作出任何承诺。因此，特斯拉起诉的是一个从未作出的承诺。最高法院不认同这一观点，裁定特斯拉有真实的前景证明，当专利所有者集体授权时，其仍受其承诺约束，且唯一的FRAND许可证是池中包括InterDigital英国专利的许可证，费率由法院设定。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The UK Supreme Court this morning unanimously revived Tesla's challenge to the royalty charged by the Avanci 5G licensing platform, and held along the way that the Delaware Court of Chancery is not an available forum for the dispute. Tesla, Inc. v. InterDigital Patent Holdings, Inc., [2026] UKSC 27 (27 July 2026). Lord Hamblen and Lord Kitchin wrote jointly, with Lord Sales, Lord Briggs, and Lord Burrows agreeing. The judgment reverses a divided Court of Appeal and adopts Lord Justice Arnold's dissent on essentially every point. The forum ruling is the piece likely to interest American readers most. Tesla's parent, both InterDigital entities, and Avanci are all US companies, the defendants offered to submit to Chancery in Del., but the Court still concluded that Delaware was unavailable, reasoning that a US court would probably not set a FRAND rate for UK patents.

The UK Supreme Court: Created by the Constitutional Reform Act 2005 and sitting since October 2009, it took over the judicial work of the House of Lords and is the final court of appeal for civil cases from England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. It has twelve justices, styled Lord or Lady rather than Justice, and most appeals are heard by panels of five. Permission to appeal is normally decided on the papers by a panel of three, and the court below may also grant it. The Court of Appeal refused Tesla permission here; the Supreme Court granted it.

Avanci owns no standard essential patents. Rather, it runs a patent pool, which it calls a platform, acting as licensing agent for 89 companies that do (including InterDigital). Each of those companies has promised ETSI, the European body that writes the 5G specification, to license its essential patents on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms. Avanci offers vehicle makers one global license covering the whole pool at a flat per-vehicle rate (the judgment's illustration uses $32), and it has no contractual authority to license any subset. To the Court of Appeal majority, each owner promised to license its own patents on FRAND terms and promised nothing at all about the price of the bundle. Tesla was therefore suing on a promise nobody had made. The Supreme Court disagreed, holding that Tesla has a real prospect of showing that a patent owner stays bound by its commitment when it licenses collectively, and a real prospect of showing that the only FRAND license of InterDigital's UK patents in the pool is the pool license itself, at a rate the court sets.

articles.title: Two Pages of Testimony: JMOL of Anticipation in Board of Regents v. Boston Scientific
articles.content:
德克萨斯大学系统董事会诉波士顿科学公司案（2024-2062、-2063）由联邦巡回法院在2026年7月27日做出裁决，这一判决撤销了德拉瓦州陪审团4200万美元的裁决，并裁定波士顿科学公司在专利无效和侵权两个方面都可以获判胜诉。

由Taranto法官代表全体法官做出的裁决指出：(1) 德州大学的美国专利6,596,296号被一项1994年关于缓释纤维的专利所预见；(2) 波士顿科学公司的药物洗脱支架并不包含声称的“纤维”，因此不构成侵权。这是本案第二次到达联邦巡回法院，第一次是在2019年的管辖权上诉中，当时德州大学试图引用州主权以保留案件在奥斯汀审理，但未能成功。

坦率地说，被告赢得预见性判决是非常罕见的。法院仅在极端情况下才会对承担举证责任的一方做出判决，特别是在无效性需要明确且令人信服的证据的情况下。下级法院的Williams法官正是基于这一点拒绝了该动议。

在最后一个被指控的专利权利要求中，全部证据仅包括先前技术参考和波士顿科学公司专家证词的约两页记录，德州大学没有作出回应。为了通过判决赢得无效性，这些证据必须足够强大，以至于陪审团不得不相信它们，无效性是唯一一个合理的陪审团能够得出的结论。

这一决定与近年来联邦巡回法院频繁推翻陪审团裁决的案例一致。2025年9月29日，Dennis Crouch在Patently-O上撰文质疑联邦巡回法院是否以违宪的方式取代了陪审团。今年，这个问题在Finesse Wireless LLC诉AT&T Mobility LLC案（25-953）中提交到最高法院，质疑联邦巡回法院是否可以仅凭冷记录来质疑陪审团对专家可信度的评估。最高法院在6月拒绝了这一案件的受理。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

Board of Regents of the University of Texas System v. Boston Scientific Corp., Nos. 2024-2062, -2063 (Fed. Cir. July 27, 2026), erases a $42 million Delaware jury verdict and holds that Boston Scientific was entitled to judgment as a matter of law on both invalidity and infringement.

Judge Taranto wrote for a unanimous panel, finding (1) UT's U.S. Patent No. 6,596,296 is anticipated by a 1994 patent on gradual-release fibers; and (2) Boston Scientific's drug-eluting stent does not contain the claimed "fiber" and so does not infringe. This is the second time the dispute has reached the Federal Circuit; the first was the 2019 venue appeal, where UT tried and failed to invoke state sovereignty to keep the case in Austin. Dennis Crouch, Sovereign Indignity: Texas must Litigate its Infringement Case in Delaware, Patently-O (Sept. 6, 2019).

To be honest, it is a bit wild for a defendant to win JMOL of anticipation. Courts grant JMOL to a party bearing the burden of proof only in extreme cases, particularly so here where invalidity requires clear and convincing evidence.  District Court Judge Williams denied the motion below on that very ground.

On the last of the four asserted claims, the entire body of evidence was the prior art reference and roughly two transcript pages from Boston Scientific's expert, with nothing in response from UT.  In order to win invalidity on JMOL, that evidence should have been so strong that the jury was not at liberty to disbelieve it, leaving invalidity as the only conclusion a reasonable juror could reach.

This decision aligns with the many examples of the past few years of the Federal Circuit freeing itself to set aside jury verdicts. See Dennis Crouch, EcoFactor: Did the Federal Circuit Unconstitutionally Displace the Jury?, Patently-O (Sept. 29, 2025). The Seventh Amendment objection to the practice reached the Supreme Court this term in Finesse Wireless LLC v. AT&T Mobility LLC, No. 25-953, asking whether the Federal Circuit may second-guess a jury’s assessment of expert credibility on a cold record. The Court denied certiorari in June.

articles.title: A Cleaner Test Case: Why Kahoot! Adds Fire to the Supreme Court’s Settled Expectations Docket
articles.content:
美国专利商标局（USPTO）的"既得期望"（settled expectations）政策现面临第二起最高法院挑战。2026年7月24日，Kahoot! AS向最高法院递交了证据申请书（证据申请书编号待定），要求法院复核联邦巡回法院在In re Kahoot! AS案件中的裁决（No. 2026-119, 2026 WL 519635 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 25, 2026)），这是一份由大法官Taranto、Mayer和Stark签署的简短强制令否决书。该申请书提出了与Google LLC v. VirtaMove Corp.（No. 25-1230）案中相同的两个问题。

Kahoot!的代理律师是Paul Hastings律师事务所的Igor Timofeyev，与Naveen Modi和Rudy Kim一起共同代理。Google的申请书由Munger Tolles律师事务所的Ginger Anders提交。Kahoot!请求法院批准并合并这两起案件，或暂缓处理Kahoot!的申请书，等待Google案的结果。[Kahoot – Certiorari Petition with appendix.]

我曾在Google申请书递交时以及5月下旬七份支持意见书到达时分别撰文评论。专利商标局放弃了答辩，但最高法院要求专利商标局作出回应。总检察长获准将答辩期限延长至2026年8月12日，而VirtaMove于7月13日提交了反对意见书。最高法院要求答辩并不保证任何结果，但至少表明法院有成员希望政府在申请决定之前辩护该政策。两起案件在"既得期望"方面也存在关键事实差异：Google案中挑战的专利已生效14年以上，而Kahoot!案中的目标专利在IPR请求书提交之日尚不满6岁。

"既得期望"这一概念在2025年3月时任代理局长Coke Morgan Stewart的临时工作负荷备忘录中进入PTAB实践，将"当事人的既得期望，如专利权利要求生效的时间长度"列为自由裁量拒绝考虑因素之一。同年6月，出于与《专利法》第286节的类比，即侵权损害赔偿仅限于起诉前6年，形成了6年的基准。

在IPR条款中，国会仅一次使用了专利年龄，作为门槛而非上限：请求人必须等待专利颁发后9个月才能提交请求，此后法律未规定专利何时不再面临挑战。Kahoot!向法院解释，被控侵权人通常没有理由研究一项专利，更不用说挑战它，直到收到诉状，这就是为什么《专利法》第315节中的一年诉讼期从送达诉状之日起开始计算。

所有这些都处于更大的结构性变化中：立案不再是委员会的决定。请求方认为这加剧了问题，因为立案现在取决于一位官员的自由裁量权，通过无解释的通知进行，并由《专利法》第314节保护免受审查。

强制令的高墙。联邦巡回法院2月的裁决没有创造任何新法律。依赖Mylan Laboratories Ltd. v. Janssen Pharmaceutica, N.V., 989 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2021)案和Apple Inc. v. Squires案（___ F.4th ___, 2026 WL 406495 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 13, 2026)），该小组认为《专利法》第314节的"最终且不可上诉"的命令通常使强制令不可用，除非有可信的宪法索赔，而超越权限（ultra vires）的论点"不能成为批准强制令请求的依据"。Kahoot!的裁决是该法院在2026年2月下旬一周内颁布的五份强制令否决之一。见Dennis Crouch, Five Petitions, Five Denials: The Federal Circuit’s Mandamus Wall Grows Higher, Patently-O (Feb. 28, 2026)。

第二份请求书增加了什么？除了"我也是"之外，Kahoot!为法院提供了一个更清晰和更激进的规则应用案例。在Google案中，一项已生效14年的专利至少超出任何合理范围。而Kahoot!的专利在请求书提交时不足6岁；该机构通过以自身决定日期为准达到6岁，该请求书批评这是双重任意的，既任意以"6年期限"为标准，又从错误的日期开始计算。如果期望可以在请求等待裁决期间得到安定，那么6年因素开始看起来不像是一个灵活的考虑因素，而更像是该机构自行制定的诉讼时效规定。

我认为，可复核性问题是证据申请的更强候选项。法定权限问题很有趣，但只有当某个法院能够达到这一问题时，它才有意义。根据联邦巡回法院的现行框架，《专利法》第314节禁止上诉，Mylan案禁止强制令，这意味着Cuozzo案中关于行政行为超越法定限制的保留描述了一种实际上任何法院都无法进行的复核形式。

政府对Google案的回应期限为8月12日，Kahoot!的请求书应在未来几天获得案件编号。如果法院要求对Kahoot!的请求书作出回应，那么当法官们在9月底的长期会议中返回时，两份请求书都将准备就绪。

这项专利是美国专利号10,339,825号"在线学术竞赛系统及方法"，由芝加哥一家名为Interstellar Inc.的小公司所有，该公司运营AreteLabs测验竞赛平台。根据起诉书，创始人Timothy Kelley于2008年在担任高中母校划船教练志愿者时构思了这一想法，并致力于将学术体育的特点（联赛、赛程、实时计分）融入课堂测验；该公司旗舰活动Math Madness模仿了NCAA锦标赛，每年吸引约2.5万名用户。

代表性权利要求1涵盖了一个包含问题数据库和处理器的系统，该处理器组建团队和联赛，发送有时间限制的测验问题，并显示"实时记分板带时钟"，记录个人和团队在实时或异步比赛中的得分。该申请于2012年4月4日提交，专利于2019年7月2日颁发，经过7年的审查程序。

诉讼。Interstellar于2024年6月起诉了Kahoot!挪威母公司及其位于奥斯汀的美国子公司。Interstellar Inc. v. Kahoot! EDU, Inc., No. 1:24-cv-00727-ADA (W.D. Tex.). 起诉书称Kahoot!平台侵犯了'825专利的8项权利要求，并指向近年来添加的团队模式和领奖台计分等功能，指控Kahoot!在2024年初Kelley与Kahoot!高管的交流中提及该专利，构成故意侵权。

中止之争。地区法院中止了诉讼以等待IPR结果，这一问题已成为双方的争议焦点。在强制令否决后，Interstellar聘请了新的诉讼律师并申请排定程序，但Albright法官于3月拒绝了该申请，但保留了提交状态报告的义务。与此同时，Kahoot!尝试了另一种行政途径，并请求对'825专利的其他权利要求进行单方面再审，但该办公室拒绝了这一请求。

Interstellar称Kahoot!在IPR、局长复核、强制令和再审中均失败，指控其"拖延"，并指出Google v. VirtaMove案的基础诉讼在加州北区未中止进行；Kahoot!回应称其上诉权尚未枯竭，并请求法院在其证据申请书得到解决前至少保持中止状态。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The USPTO’s “settled expectations” policy now has a second challenger at the Supreme Court. On July 24, 2026, Kahoot! AS filed a petition for certiorari (docket number pending) asking the Court to review the Federal Circuit’s order in In re Kahoot! AS, No. 2026-119, 2026 WL 519635 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 25, 2026), a two-page per curiam mandamus denial from Judges Taranto, Mayer, and Stark. The petition presents the same two questions already pending in Google LLC v. VirtaMove, Corp., No. 25-1230:

  1. Whether the agency has statutory authority to deny inter partes review institution based on a patent’s age, given that Congress set a nine-month minimum age for IPR petitions but no maximum; and
  2. Whether 35 U.S.C. § 314(d) bars judicial review, even by way of mandamus, when a denial rests on grounds contrary to the statute.

Igor Timofeyev of Paul Hastings is counsel of record, joined by Naveen Modi and Rudy Kim. Ginger Anders of Munger Tolles filed the Google petition. Kahoot! asks the Court to grant and consolidate the two cases, or alternatively to hold its petition for Google. [Kahoot – Certiorari Petition with appendix.]

I wrote about the Google petition when it was filed and again when seven amicus briefs arrived in late May. The PTO waived its response, but the Court requested a response. The Solicitor General obtained an extension to August 12, 2026, while VirtaMove went ahead and filed its brief in opposition on July 13. A call for a response is no guarantee of anything, but it means at least someone at the Court wants the government to defend the policy before the petition is resolved. The two cases also offer a key factual difference with regard to settled expectations: Google’s challenged patents had been in force for more than fourteen years, while Kahoot!’s target was less than six years old on the day the IPR petition was filed.

Settled expectations entered PTAB practice through then-Acting Director Coke Morgan Stewart’s March 2025 interim workload memorandum, which listed “settled expectations of the parties, such as the length of time the claims have been in force” among the considerations for discretionary denial. The six-year benchmark emerged that June with an analogy to 35 U.S.C. § 286, which limits infringement damages to the six years before suit.

Congress used patent age exactly once in the IPR provisions, as a floor rather than a ceiling: a petitioner must wait for nine months after issuance to file, and after that the statute says nothing about a patent ever becoming too old to challenge. Kahoot! explains to the Court that an accused infringer often has no reason to study a patent, much less challenge it, until the complaint arrives, which is why the one-year litigation deadline of § 315(b) runs from service of the complaint.

All this is sitting within a larger structural shift: institution is no longer a Board decision. Petitioners argue that this has exacerbated the problem because institution now turns on one official’s discretion, exercised through unexplained notices and shielded from review by § 314(d).

The mandamus wall. The Federal Circuit’s February order broke no new ground. Relying on Mylan Laboratories Ltd. v. Janssen Pharmaceutica, N.V., 989 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2021), and its precedential decision in Apple Inc. v. Squires, ___ F.4th ___, 2026 WL 406495 (Fed. Cir. Feb. 13, 2026), the panel held that § 314(d)’s “final and nonappealable” command leaves mandamus ordinarily unavailable absent a colorable constitutional claim, and that ultra vires arguments “cannot be a basis for granting the petition for mandamus.” The Kahoot! order was one of five mandamus denials the court issued in a single week in late February. See Dennis Crouch, Five Petitions, Five Denials: The Federal Circuit’s Mandamus Wall Grows Higher, Patently-O (Feb. 28, 2026).

What does a second petition add? Beyond a “me too,” Kahoot! offers the Court a cleaner and more aggressive application of the rule. In Google, a fourteen-year-old patent at least sits comfortably past any plausible line. Kahoot!’s patent was under six when the petition was filed; the agency reached six only by measuring age at the date of its own decision, a move the petition calls arbitrary twice over, both for the “arbitrary period of six years” itself and for measuring from the wrong date. If expectations can settle while a petition awaits a ruling, the six-year factor starts to look less like one flexible consideration and more like a statute of repose that the agency wrote for itself.

This is a situation where, I believe, the reviewability question is the stronger candidate for certiorari. The statutory authority question is interesting, but it only matters if some court can ever reach it. Under the Federal Circuit’s current framework, § 314(d) bars appeal and Mylan bars mandamus, which means the Cuozzo reservation for agency action exceeding statutory limits describes a form of review that no court can actually conduct.

The government’s response in Google is due August 12, and the Kahoot! petition should receive its docket number in the coming days. If the Court calls for a response here as well, both petitions will be ready for the Justices when they return for the long conference at the end of September.

= = =

The patent. The patent behind all of this is U.S. Patent No. 10,339,825, “System and Method for On-Line Academic Competition,” owned by Interstellar Inc., a small Chicago company that runs the AreteLabs quiz-competition platform. According to the complaint, founder Timothy Kelley conceived the idea in 2008 while volunteering as a rowing coach at his high school alma mater and set out to bring the trappings of scholastic sports (leagues, brackets, real time scoring) into classroom quizzing; the company’s flagship event, Math Madness, is patterned on the NCAA tournament, and the platform draws about 25,000 subscribers a year.

Representative claim 1 covers a system with a question database and a processor that assembles teams and leagues, delivers timed quiz questions, and displays a “real time scoreboard with time clock” tallying individual and team scores in live or asynchronous matches. The application was filed April 4, 2012, and the patent issued July 2, 2019, after seven years in prosecution.

The lawsuit. Interstellar sued both the Kahoot! Norwegian parent and its Austin-based U.S. subsidiary in June 2024. Interstellar Inc. v. Kahoot! EDU, Inc., No. 1:24-cv-00727-ADA (W.D. Tex.). The complaint asserts eight claims of the ‘825 patent against the Kahoot! platform – pointing to features added over the years such as team mode and podium scoring, and alleges willful infringement based on early 2024 correspondence in which Kelley raised the patent with a Kahoot! executive.

The stay fight. The district court stayed litigation awaiting the IPR outcome – and that issue has become a battleground for the parties. After the mandamus denial, Interstellar brought in new litigation counsel and moved for a scheduling order, which Judge Albright denied without prejudice in March while keeping the status-report obligations in place. Meanwhile, Kahoot! tried the other administrative track and requested ex parte reexamination of additional claims of the ‘825 patent – but the office denied that request.

Interstellar says Kahoot! has now lost the IPR, Director Review, mandamus, and the reexam, accuses it of “stalling,” and points out that the underlying Google v. VirtaMove litigation is proceeding unstayed in the Northern District of California; Kahoot! answers that its appellate rights are not exhausted and asks the court to hold the stay in place at least until its cert petition is resolved.
